requirement: Each file entry pairs its assigned root ID with the domain identity serialized as a JSON value. The whole entry is a valid node argument under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.node_reference.consistency`. Follow `next` to retrieve further pages.
rationale:
I judged the tests adequate for all three clauses of `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.list_sources.behavior`. I judged this from the supplied test source and did not request any implementation source.

**1. Each entry pairs its assigned root ID with the domain identity serialized as JSON.**
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[listing_continuations_return_complete_paths_from_the_original_listing]` calls `list_sources` and walks every page. Each entry's `node` is deserialized as a `NodeId<Project>`.
- The test asserts that `entry["data"]` equals the identity the cache holds for that node (`tools.domain.cache().node_data(node)`).
- It also asserts that the collected IDs equal `intern_node(format!("{file}#"))` for each file, in order. That checks the IDs are the ones assigned to the files.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/configured.rs#mod[tests]/fn[configured_agent_uses_domain_source_tools_in_independent_executions]` asserts that every listing entry has an integer `node` and an integer `data.id`.

**2. The whole entry is a valid node argument under `node_reference.consistency`.**
- The same `configured.rs` test takes the listing entry at the selected index and passes it unchanged as the arguments of `read_node`. The call succeeds and returns the mapped snapshot text. This shows a `node` plus `data` entry is accepted.
- It runs twice, in independent executions.
- The error cases for mismatched, unassigned or malformed data belong to the cited `node_reference.consistency`, so they need no test here.

**3. Follow `next` to retrieve further pages.**
- The `project_sources.rs` test lists 2000 files, so the listing spans several pages. It asserts that the first page has a string `next`.
- It follows `next` through `get_next_page` until none is left and compares the concatenated IDs with the full expected list. A listing that dropped, duplicated or reordered entries across pages would fail.
- The test adds a file after the first page and still expects the original list. This confirms continuations come from the original listing.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[source_discovery_and_its_pages_do_not_register_reads]` also follows `next` for `list_sources`.

**Supporting tests.** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/source_defaults.rs#fn[gitignore_is_shared_by_all_operations_with_or_without_a_git_repository]` and `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[source_tools_forward_arguments_and_present_discovery_and_read_results]` are marked against this requirement and add listing coverage. They cover which files appear and how `list_sources` forwards its arguments. They support the main tests but are not needed for the three clauses.

I found no gap.

text: Each file entry pairs its assigned root ID with the domain identity serialized as a JSON value. The whole entry is a valid node argument under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.node_reference.consistency`. Follow `next` to retrieve further pages.

A tool MUST also accept `node` and `data` together. Look up the existing ID and compare its stored identity with the deserialized `data` using `D::NodeData` equality. Use that ID on a match. An unassigned ID, malformed data, or a mismatch produces a tool error, even if the supplied data would be valid on its own. A `path` address may include `location` and must be used separately from `node` and `data`.
